periods.title: Uttar Pradesh in 21st Century
periods.tagline: Viksit Uttar Pradesh Is the Foundation of Viksit Bharat
periods.overview: The 21st century has been a period of transformation for Uttar Pradesh — with its large population, strategic location and rich heritage, the state plays a crucial role in India's growth story. With India's largest population (per Census 2011, about 18% of the national total), the 2nd largest state economy, leadership in foodgrain and sugarcane production, and a rapidly expanding infrastructure and investment base, U.P. increasingly positions itself as an engine of India's growth, while continuing to work through challenges of regional disparity, urban congestion and human development gaps.

phases.name: Economic Growth & Development
points: GSDP (current prices): ₹20.51 lakh crore, 2nd in India; share in India's GSDP: approx. 8.6%; per capita income: approx. ₹46,817, below the national average

NSDP growth rate (2023–24): 12.8%, 1st among large states; FDI inflow (Apr 2000–Dec 2023): US$20+ Billion, a top state; Ease of Doing Business Rank 2020: 2nd; strong growth in services, manufacturing, IT/ITeS and exports

phases.name: Industry, Investment & Infrastructure
points: Industrial corridors — DMIC, Bundelkhand, Purvanchal Expressway, Ganga Expressway; major sectors — electronics, food processing, textile, leather, furniture, defence, handicrafts

'One District One Product' (ODOP) is a flagship programme; thriving start-up ecosystem (Lucknow, Noida, Kanpur, Varanasi hubs); regular Investors Summits — U.P. Global Investors Summit; expressways, dedicated freight corridors, Vande Bharat trains, international airports (Noida/Jewar, Kushinagar); power-surplus state with a focus on solar and renewable energy

phases.name: Governance, Social Justice & Culture
points: Focus on transparent, accountable, technology-driven governance — e-District, online services, DigiLocker, Jan Suvidha Kendras; Swachh Bharat Mission, Mission Shakti (women's safety & empowerment); law & order modernisation — 112, CCTNS, e-FIR

Social justice & welfare schemes — PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, Ayushman Bharat, Mission Shakti, Kanya Sumangala Yojana, Antyodaya Anna Yojana; culture & heritage — development of the Ramayana, Buddhist and Krishna spiritual circuits, Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, Ayodhya Dham, Mathura-Vrindavan Corridor, Prayagraj Mahakumbh (2019, 2025)

Social Development and Human Capital: Education: improvement in enrolment, especially of girls, through 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao', Samagra Shiksha, Mission Prerna; Health: expansion of CHCs, PHCs, medical colleges, Ayushman Bharat, Jan Aushadhi Kendras
Skill Development: Kaushal Vikas Mission, ITIs modernisation, focus on youth employability; Digital Inclusion: BharatNet, Common Service Centres (CSCs), digital payments & DBT
Urbanization, Environment & Sustainable: Rapid urbanisation with planned development; Smart City Mission projects in Lucknow, Kanpur, Varanasi, Agra, Prayagraj; Metro Rail — Lucknow, Kanpur, Agra, Noida-Greater Noida; AMRUT, Housing for All, SBM-U 2.0

Afforestation and increase in green cover; Namami Gange Programme — Ganga rejuvenation; promotion of renewable energy (Solar Policy); waste management, solid & liquid waste handling; climate change adaptation — flood control, drought management, water conservation
Major Challenges: Unemployment and underemployment; regional disparities (Purvanchal, Bundelkhand); low per capita income; population pressure and urban congestion; farm distress, land fragmentation; environmental degradation and pollution; quality of education and health services; women's safety and social issues
Way Forward: Balanced regional development — Purvanchal & Bundelkhand; quality education, skill development and innovation; industrialisation with sustainability and green growth; agricultural diversification and value addition; strengthening health, nutrition and social protection
Good governance, digital transformation and citizen-centric services; inclusive growth ensuring 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas'

periods.title: Important Cities & Personalities of Uttar Pradesh
periods.tagline: From the Banks of the Ganga to the Fields of Awadh, from Ancient Sages to Modern Leaders, Uttar Pradesh Has Always Been a Land of Ideas, Courage and Contribution to India's Journey
periods.overview: A cross-cutting reference companion to the rest of the Uttar Pradesh track: a gallery of the state's defining cities and of the men and women — from mythological and Vedic figures through medieval rulers and reformers to modern political leaders, freedom fighters, scientists and artists — whose lives are most frequently drawn on in UPPSC's History, Art & Culture, and Society questions. Because this page spans every era, it functions as a hub: almost every name here also has a fuller biography or period on this site.

phases.name: Mythological & Vedic Figures
points: Lord Rama (Ayodhya) — ideal ruler, Maryada Purushottam, symbol of dharma; Lord Krishna (Mathura) — pivotal role in the Mahabharata, symbol of wisdom & diplomacy
Gargi Vachaknavi, Maitreyi (associated with Vedic learning centres) — Vedic scholars & philosophers who participated in debates and are known for their philosophical wisdom

phases.name: Ancient & Early Medieval Figures
points: Chanakya (Kautilya, 4th century BCE) — political thinker, author of the Arthashastra, associate of Chandragupta Maurya; Ashoka (born in Lumbini, associated with U.P., 3rd century BCE) — Mauryan emperor, propagated Buddhism, dharma & welfare
Harsha Vardhana (Kanauj, 7th century CE) — mighty ruler of Kanauj, patron of learning & Buddhism

phases.name: Medieval Figures
points: Goswami Tulsidas (16th century) — author of the Ramcharitmanas, devotee poet of Lord Rama; Raja Todar Mal (16th century) — finance minister of Akbar, land revenue reforms

Razia Sultan (13th century, associated with Badaun) — ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, known for her courage; Rani Durgavati (16th century, associated with Bundelkhand) — Gond queen who fought against Mughal forces bravely; Jahanara Begum (17th century, associated with Agra) — Mughal princess, philanthropist, builder of sarais & bazaars; Ahilyabai Holkar (18th century, associated with the Kashi corridor) — Holkar queen who built ghats in Varanasi and many temples

phases.name: 19th Century Figures
points: Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow) — leader of the 1857 revolt in Awadh, symbol of courage; Nana Saheb Peshwa (Dhondu Pant) — key leader of the 1857 revolt in Kanpur; Mangal Pandey (Ballia) — freedom fighter associated with the 1857 revolt

Rani Lakshmibai (Allahabad & Jhansi) — brave warrior of the 1857 revolt, symbol of valour and sacrifice; Uda Devi Pasi (Lucknow) — brave freedom fighter of the 1857 revolt; Pt. Madan Mohan Malaviya (Prayagraj, 19th–20th century) — freedom fighter, founder of BHU, champion of education

phases.name: 20th–21st Century Figures
points: Chandra Shekhar Azad (Allahabad), Govind Ballabh Pant (Allahabad) — freedom fighter, first CM of U.P.; Dr. Sampurnanand (Varanasi); Atal Bihari Vajpayee (Gwalior-born, associated with U.P.) — former PM of India, poet, statesman

Sarojini Naidu (Prayagraj), Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit (Allahabad), Sucheta Kripalani (Lucknow) — freedom fighter, first woman CM of U.P.; Mulayam Singh Yadav (Etawah), Mayawati (Delhi, active in U.P.), Yogi Adityanath (Pauri Garhwal, associated with Gorakhpur) — political leaders of independent India's U.P.; Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam (Rameswaram, long associated with U.P. through work at DRDO) — former President of India

Ayodhya — birthplace of Lord Ram, ancient cultural & religious centre; Varanasi — one of the world's oldest living cities, spiritual capital of India; Prayagraj (Allahabad) — confluence of Triveni, Kumbh Mela, centre of freedom struggle; Mathura — birthplace of Lord Krishna, important religious and cultural centre

Sarnath — the Buddha delivered his first sermon here, important Buddhist site; Kanpur — major industrial city, role in the freedom struggle, centre of leather & textiles; Lucknow — capital of Awadh, centre of culture, art, architecture & education; Agra — home to the Taj Mahal, major Mughal centre, tourism & industry hub; Jhansi — historical fort, symbol of resistance & valour in 1857; Meerut — birthplace of the 1857 revolt, major cantonment city
Personalities — Sports, Literature, Art: Sports: Major Dhyan Chand (Allahabad) — hockey wizard, Bharat Ratna; Vijay Singh (Ghazipur) — golfer; Saina Nehwal (associated with U.P.) — badminton champion

Literature: Munshi Premchand (Varanasi) — novelist, Godan, Nirmala; Harivansh Rai Bachchan (Prayagraj) — poet, Madhushala; Amritlal Nagar (Agra) — novelist, cultural chronicler; Mahadevi Verma (Farrukhabad) — poet, modern Hindi literature stalwart
Art & Music: Bismillah Khan (Dumraon, U.P.) — shehnai maestro, Bharat Ratna; Ravi Shankar (Varanasi) — sitar maestro, Bharat Ratna; Pt. Birju Maharaj (Lucknow) — Kathak exponent

Spiritual & Reformers: Swami Vivekananda (visited Kashi); Swami Ramanand (Varanasi) — Bhakti reformer; Saint Kabir (Varanasi) — Bhakti poet, social reformer; Saint Ravidas (Varanasi) — Bhakti saint, social equality
Science & Others: Dr. Har Gobind Khorana (Raipur, U.P. origin) — Nobel Laureate; Homi Bhabha (born in Mumbai, father from Allahabad) — Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme
Freedom Struggle Heroes of U.P. at a Gla: Leaders of the 1857 Revolt: Nana Saheb, Rani Lakshmibai, Begum Hazrat Mahal, Kunwar Singh (Bihar, associated with U.P. areas), Mangal Pandey
Revolutionaries: Chandra Shekhar Azad, Ram Prasad Bismil (Shahjahanpur), Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh, Sachindra Nath Sanyal

Kisan Leaders: Baba Ramchandra (Awadh Kisan Movement), Swami Sahajanand Saraswati (Kisan leader); Gandhian Leaders: Govind Ballabh Pant, Purushottam Das Tandon, Jawaharlal Nehru (associated with Allahabad), Brahm Dutt Dwivedi
